title: Relativity Cosmology
Unifying Special and General Relativity Through Universal Relativity
abstract: This publication has been amended to correct a mathematical formulation in the general relativity equation, please see publication: 10.5281/zenodo.15011480   This paper proposes a unification of Special and General Relativity through the framework of Universal Relativity (UR). By incorporating scale-dependent transformations, we demonstrate that both the time dilation of Special Relativity and the gravitational time dilation of General Relativity can be derived from a single scaling equation. This approach resolves apparent contradictions in gravitational time dilation and provides a unified perspective on relativistic effects.

title: Anti Einstein – Refutation of Einstein's General Theory of Relativity
abstract: More than ninety years after publication, Einstein's general relativity theory is still a highly successful theory of gravitation. Meanwhile, general relativity theory has passed a lot of observational and experimental tests, opportunities to test the validity of general relativity are increasing. Yet more and more, some recent observational data (dark energy) indicate the need to test the logical consistency of Einstein's general relativity theory. The present investigation will refute Einstein's general relativity theory by the proof that Einstein's general relativity theory is not a complete physical theory .

title: Dynamic sources, Dynamic Multi-folds, and General Relativity Lense-Thirring and Frame Dragging Effects
abstract: In a multi-fold universe, gravity emerges from entanglement through the multi-fold mechanisms. As a result, gravity-like effects appear in between entangled particles, whether they are real or virtual. Long range, massless gravity results from entanglement of massless virtual particles. Entanglement of massive virtual particles leads to massive gravity contributions at very smalls scales. Multi-folds mechanisms also result into a spacetime that is discrete, with a random walk fractal structure, and non-commutative geometry, which is Lorentz invariant, and where spacetime nodes, and particles, can be modeled with microscopic black holes. All these recover General Relativity (GR) at large scales, and semi-classical model remain valid till smaller scale than usually expected. Gravity can therefore be added to the Standard Model (SM) resulting into what we define as SM G . This can contribute to resolving several open issues with the Standard Model without new Physics other than gravity, as well as to open issues with the Standard Cosmological Model   The paper discusses how multi-folds apply when sources of gravity, or the center of mass of entangled systems, are dynamically moving: multi-folds mechanisms remain the same but using the evolving center of mass. As a result gravity, or gravity-like, contributions are to be vectorially integrated over the retarded multi-fold spacetime location that can contribute to a point at a certain time (spacetime location), instead of all the multi-folds for all directions. It is illustrated in the case of a rotating sphere as source of gravity: we recover the Lense-Thirring results with its centripetal, Coriolis and axial contributions. The analysis allows us to settle contradictory, and incorrect, results encountered in the literature. It also shows how non-linearity of General Relativity (GR) appears in the multi-fold mechanisms, something that may not have been obvious to all in the original papers. The ability for the multi-fold mechanisms to explain such GR effects help better understand these effects, but more importantly, it is another way to illustrate and validate that multi-folds recover GR and GR recovers the multi-folds.

title: A DISCUSSION ABOUT TIME DILATION BASED ON SPECIAL RELATIVITY
abstract: This article discusses time dilation based on special relativity. An experiment is designed to examine time dilation effects deduced from special relativity. This experiment is similar to but different from the famous “twin paradox” because this experiment doesn’t involve any accelerating process, or decelerating process, or change of travelling directions. Impossible results of the experiment are deduced by using special relativity. Thus it can be concluded that the theory of relativity (special relativity) is incorrect.
keywords: Special Relativity, Theory of Relativity, Albert Einstein, Speed of Light, Frame of Reference, Theoretical Physics, Time Dilation, Space Travel & Time Expansion

title: ABSOLUTE SIMULTANEITY REDEFINED
abstract: ABSOLUTE SIMULTANEITY REDEFINED "... no longer a coordinate artifact ( arte factum ), but a physical fact ( factum ) — twins of Latin facere , though only the latter is granted reality by nature. " Absolute (adj.) A monadic, invariant geometric property of an object's state relative to the background manifold; recovered from the underlying  spacetime structure and preserved across coordinate transformations. Not arising from a dyadic relation to arbitrary inertial frames.   At the beginning of the twentieth century, physics underwent a radical change in its understanding of space and time. In 1904, Hendrik Lorentz refined the transformation laws that would later bear his name, showing how electromagnetic phenomena could retain their form for bodies moving through the ether. In 1905, Albert Einstein took the decisive conceptual step: he removed the need for an undetectable ether and grounded relativity in operational measurements made with clocks, rods, and light signals. Simultaneity, in Einstein’s formulation, was no longer absolute. It depended on how observers in relative motion synchronized distant clocks with light pulses in their respective inertial frames. Then, in 1908, Hermann Minkowski gave Einstein’s theory its geometric form. Space by itself and time by itself, Minkowski declared, were “doomed to fade away into mere shadows”; only their union would preserve independent reality. Relativity was no longer merely a theory of moving observers. It became a theory of spacetime. Absolute Simultaneity Redefined begins from that historical turning point. This book does not reject Einstein’s relativity, alter the Lorentz transformation, or add new physical laws. Instead, it asks whether Minkowski spacetime contains more recoverable structure than the standard interpretation usually assigns to it. If the time experienced by an object along its path through spacetime is fixed by invariant geometry, can time dilation be understood as absolute, monadic, and spacetime-geometric? And if spacetime itself is the deeper reality, can a determinate simultaneity relation be recovered from its own geometric structure without returning to Newtonian absolute time or an ether-like preferred frame? Daniel William Ho develops this question through the theory of the Law of Relativity and Absolutes and the theoretical framework of the Privileged Frame. In this framework, the absolute is not space alone or time alone, but a geometric property recovered from the spacetime manifold. Beginning with Minkowski’s spacetime picture, the book revisits the hyperboloidal geometry of Lorentz transformations: a 3+1-dimensional spacetime structure in which each admissible timelike direction defines a possible simultaneity hypersurface. Once such a hypersurface is selected, the construction turns to the ellipsoidal spatial geometry within it. This geometry is not separate from relativity; it arises from the Minkowski metric as measured on the spacelike hypersurface orthogonal to the chosen timelike direction. The Privileged Frame is recovered where that direction defines a simultaneity hypersurface on which spatial relations, timing relations, and physical correlations can be assigned a common geometric footing. From there, the book moves beyond flat spacetime. Special Relativity serves as the foundation, but not the limit. The Privileged Frame is developed as a recovered foliation whose significance extends into curved geometry, quantum coherence, and phase-sensitive correlations. The aim is not to replace General Relativity or quantum mechanics, but to ask whether a common geometric timing structure can clarify where observer-dependent description ends and physical correlation begins. The result is a reinterpretation of relativity’s most famous lesson. Simultaneity remains relative under Einstein’s original synchronization convention. But from the physical structure of spacetime itself, this book asks whether simultaneity may also possess a deeper, recoverable meaning. From Lorentz’s transformations, to Einstein’s clocks, to Minkowski’s spacetime, this book follows the historical path of relativity—and then asks a question still open to interpretation at its foundations: Is time merely a coordinate assignment, or can it also be recovered as a physical relation within spacetime geometry itself—where even Einstein’s “spooky action at a distance” may find a deeper geometric meaning?

title: Complete Solution of the Einstein Field Equations for a Spherical Distribution of Polytropic Matter
abstract: We determine the complete solution of the Einstein field equations for the case of a spherically symmetric distribution of gaseous matter, characterized by a polytropic equation of state. We show that the field equations automatically generate two sharp boundaries for the gas, an inner one and an outer one, given by radial positions r1 and r2, and thus define a shell of gaseous matter outside of which the energy density is exactly zero. Hence this shell is surrounded by an outer vacuum region, and surrounds an inner vacuum region. Therefore, the solution is given in three regions, one being the well-known analytical Schwarzschild exterior solution in the outer vacuum region, one being determined analytically in the inner vacuum region, and one being determined partially analytically and partially numerically, within the matter region, between the two boundary values r1 and r2 of the Schwarzschild radial coordinate r. This solution is therefore somewhat similar to the one previously found for a spherically symmetric shell of liquid fluid, and is in fact exactly the same in the cases of the inner and outer vacuum regions. The main difference is that here the boundary values r1 and r2 are not chosen arbitrarily, but are instead determined by the dynamics of the system. As was shown in the case of the liquid shell, also in this solution there is a singularity at the origin, that just as in that case does not correspond to an infinite concentration of matter, but in fact to zero matter energy density at the center. Also as in the case of the liquid shell, the spacetime within the spherical cavity is not flat, so that there is a non-trivial gravitational field there, in contrast with Newtonian gravitation. This inner gravitational field has the effect of repelling matter and energy away from the origin, thus avoiding a concentration of matter at that point.
keywords: General Relativity, Einstein Equations, Boundary Conditions, Polytropes.

title: Exact Solution of the Einstein Field Equations for a Spherical Shell of Fluid Matter
abstract: We determine the exact solution of the Einstein field equations for the case of a spherically symmetric shell of liquid matter, characterized by an energy density which is constant with the Schwarzschild radial coordinate r between two values r1 and r2. The solution is given in three regions, one being the well-known analytical Schwarzschild solution in the outer vacuum region, one being determined analytically in the inner vacuum region, and one being determined mostly analytically but partially numerically, within the matter region. The solutions for the temporal coefficient of the metric and for the pressure within this region are given in terms of a non-elementary but fairly straightforward real integral. For some values of the parameters this integral can be written in terms of elementary functions. We show that in this solution there is a singularity at the origin, and give the parameters of that singularity in terms of the geometrical and physical parameters of the shell. This does not correspond to an infinite concentration of matter, but in fact to zero energy density at the center. It does, however, imply that the spacetime within the spherical cavity is not flat, so that there is a non-trivial gravitational field there, in contrast with Newtonian gravitation. This gravitational field is repulsive with respect to the origin, and thus has the effect of stabilizing the geometrical configuration of the matter, since any particle of the matter that wanders out into either one of the vacuum regions tends to be brought back to the bulk of the matter by the gravitational field.
keywords: General Relativity, Einstein Equations, Boundary Conditions, Exact Solution.

title: Revision of General Relativity Guided by Enthalpy Conservation
abstract: The theory of general relativity boasts incomparable accuracy in both predicting and explaining phenomena to which the exterior Schwarzschild solution is applicable.  However, as far as those related to the FLRW metric and the interior Schwarzschild metric are concerned, it has left with us more controversies than legacies.  In this paper, I will provide a revision of Einstein’s field equation guided by a newly proposed principle of enthalpy conservation, and present a simpler alternative theory of gravity which is compatible with Maxwellian electromagnetism.
